title: Île Flottante: Poached Meringue on Crème Anglaise
summary: Cloud-soft poached meringues floating on chilled vanilla crème anglaise, drizzled with amber caramel.

ingredients.item: whole milk, plus extra for poaching
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Crème anglaise
steps.text: infuse the milk with the vanilla seeds and pod until steaming, covered, 15 min. Whisk the yolks with the 60 g sugar, whisk in the hot milk, return to the pan and stir on low until it coats the spoon at 80-82 °C. Strain into the jug and chill. Gentle stirring to 80-82 °C cooks the yolks safely and keeps it smooth.

steps.title: Meringue
steps.text: whisk the whites with the salt and cream of tartar to foam, add the sugar gradually and whisk to firm, glossy peaks. Cream of tartar makes the meringue stable.

steps.title: Poach
steps.text: bring the poaching milk to a bare simmer, about 80 °C. Shape 6 large ovals of meringue with the two spoons and poach 2-3 at a time 2 min per side until set and springy. Drain on the paper. If the milk boils, the meringue puffs and then collapses.

steps.title: Caramel
steps.text: heat the sugar and water without stirring until deep amber, then take off the heat. Stirring can make the sugar crystallise.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: pour the cold crème anglaise into the bowls, float a meringue on each and drizzle with the caramel straight away.

tips: A common mistake is boiling the poaching milk; keep it barely trembling.
Caramel burns quickly; take it off the heat as soon as it is deep amber.
Make the crème anglaise a day ahead so it is properly cold.
storage: Best on the day. The crème anglaise keeps covered in the fridge for 2 days; keep poached meringues in the fridge for up to 4 hours.
